docs.title: dcs-bridge
docs.text: dcs-bridge est un pont générique entre DCS World et des consommateurs externes (TUI, interface web, agents IA).

docs.title: Vue d'ensemble
docs.text:
graph LR
    DCS["DCS World\n(Lua bridge)"]
    SERVE["dcs-serve\n(TCP → HTTP/WS)"]
    TUI["dcs-client tui\n(Textual TUI)"]
    WEB["dcs-client web\n(Leaflet map)"]
    MCP["dcs-client mcp\n(MCP tools)"]
    AI["Agent IA\n(Claude, GPT…)"]

    DCS -->|TCP JSON| SERVE
    SERVE -->|HTTP REST| TUI
    SERVE -->|WebSocket| TUI
    SERVE -->|HTTP REST| WEB
    SERVE -->|WebSocket| WEB
    SERVE -->|HTTP REST| MCP
    MCP -->|stdio MCP| AI

docs.title: Fonctionnalités
docs.text:
• Bridge Lua — injecté dans DCS World, envoie les positions des unités et les événements en temps réel
  • dcs-serve — serveur TCP/HTTP/WebSocket, snapshot en mémoire, authentification par clé API
  • dcs-client tui — interface terminal Textual avec tableau des unités en temps réel et REPL Lua
  • dcs-client web — carte Leaflet avec marqueurs colorés par coalition, mise à jour en temps réel
  • dcs-client mcp — serveur MCP exposant exec_lua, get_units, spawn_unit, get_mission_info

docs.title: Démarrage rapide
docs.text:
# 1. Lancer le serveur
dcs-serve

# 2. Ouvrir l'interface web (dans un autre terminal)
dcs-client web

# 3. Ou lancer le TUI
dcs-client tui

Consultez le Guide d'installation pour les instructions complètes.

docs.title: ADR-0001 : Conversion de coordonnées effectuée côté Lua
docs.text: Statut : Accepté Date : 2026-06-07

docs.title: Contexte
docs.text: Les unités DCS ont des positions en coordonnées natives DCS (système de projection plate, origine par théâtre). Les consommateurs de l'API ont besoin de lat/lon. La conversion doit se faire quelque part.

docs.title: Décision
docs.text: Le Lua bridge effectue la conversion via les API DCS natives (coord.LOtoLL(), land.getHeight()) et envoie les deux représentations dans chaque message : position_dcs et position_geo.

docs.title: Alternatives considérées
docs.text: Conversion côté Python (dcs-serve) : nécessite d'implémenter la projection par théâtre en Python (paramètres custom, non-standard). Des projets comme dcs-liberation l'ont fait, mais c'est fragile si ED modifie les paramètres, et représente un travail de maintenance non négligeable.

docs.title: Conséquences
docs.text:
• Lua envoie plus de données (~2x les coordonnées), impact négligeable sur TCP.
  • Zéro logique de projection côté Python — serve est agnostique au théâtre.
  • Fiabilité garantie : coord.LOtoLL() est l'API officielle DCS, maintenue par ED.
  • Tout nouveau théâtre DCS fonctionne sans modification de dcs-serve.

docs.title: ADR-0002 : Cache snapshot push-based dans dcs-serve
docs.text: Statut : Accepté Date : 2026-06-07

docs.title: Contexte
docs.text: GET /api/units doit répondre rapidement. Interroger DCS via TCP à chaque requête HTTP introduirait une latence de 100–5000ms (cycle de poll Lua + round-trip).

docs.title: Décision
docs.text:
dcs-serve maintient un Snapshot en mémoire mis à jour par deux mécanismes : 1. Events : le Lua bridge pousse les changements dès qu'ils arrivent. 2. Full Refresh : le Lua bridge envoie l'état complet toutes les 5 secondes.

GET /api/units sert toujours depuis le Snapshot. Si DCS est déconnecté, le Snapshot est marqué stale: true avec last_updated. Avant le premier Full Refresh, serve répond 503 { "ready": false }.

docs.title: Alternatives considérées
docs.text: Stateless pur : chaque GET /api/units déclenche un exec_lua pour lire l'état. Simple, mais latence imprévisible et charge CPU DCS proportionnelle aux clients connectés.

docs.title: Conséquences
docs.text:
• dcs-serve a un état interne — tests d'intégration nécessaires pour couvrir les cas stale/ready.
  • Les clients WebSocket reçoivent les Events en temps réel + le Full Refresh toutes les 5s pour resynchroniser.
  • La fraîcheur des données est bornée à 5s dans le pire cas (entre deux Full Refresh, sans Events).

docs.title: ADR-0003 : Reconnexion TCP Lua bridge — retry infini avec backoff exponentiel
docs.text: Statut : Accepté Date : 2026-06-07

docs.title: Contexte
docs.text:
Le Lua bridge ouvre une connexion TCP sortante vers dcs-serve. Si dcs-serve est indisponible (redémarrage, crash réseau), le bridge doit gérer la reconnexion sans bloquer la mission DCS.

Le scheduler Lua (timer.scheduleFunction) tourne dans le thread de simulation — tout blocage gèle la mission.

docs.title: Décision
docs.text:
Retry infini avec backoff exponentiel. Après N secondes sans connexion établie, un warning est émis dans le log DCS. Le backoff est plafonné à une valeur max configurable (défaut 60s). La mission continue normalement pendant les tentatives.

La socket est configurée avec un timeout très court (settimeout(0.0001)) — les appels sont non-bloquants.

docs.title: Alternatives considérées
docs.text:
Witchcraft (retry immédiat sans backoff) : retry à chaque step (100ms) — génère du bruit dans les logs et charge CPU inutile lors d'une indisponibilité longue.

Abandon après N secondes : simple, mais perd la connexion définitivement si serve redémarre plus tard. Inacceptable pour un outil de monitoring de mission longue durée.

docs.title: Conséquences
docs.text:
• La mission DCS reste jouable même si dcs-serve est absent.
  • Le log DCS signale clairement l'indisponibilité du bridge sans spammer.
  • dcs-serve peut redémarrer à tout moment — le bridge se reconnecte automatiquement.

docs.title: Backlog restructure to .backlog/ per-lot directories
docs.text: The backlog lived in a single monolithic BACKLOG.md (~24 KB). With one branch and one PR per lot (CLAUDE.md §8), the monolith was a recurring merge-conflict surface, and loading the whole file cost agent context on every task. We also wanted to drive the backlog with the Matt Pocock engineering skills (to-prd, to-issues, triage), which are issue-tracker-agnostic and configured per repo (no fork required).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Adopt a per-lot .backlog/ structure:

  • Active lots are directories — .backlog/<LOT-ID>/PRD.md plus one tickets/<NN>-<slug>.md per ticket.
  • Completed lots are compact .backlog/archive/<LOT-ID>.md files (ticket table preserved, not split).
  • A single Status: vocabulary (⬜ ready · 🔄 in-progress · 🧑 waiting-human · ✅ done · 🚫 wontfix) maps onto Matt's triage roles.
  • The Matt Pocock skills stay globally installed and unmodified; per-repo config under docs/agents/* plus an ## Agent skills block in CLAUDE.md adapts them to this backlog.
  • The lot index .backlog/README.md is maintained by hand (no generator script).
  • .backlog/ is a dotfolder: internal working state, excluded from the published MkDocs site.

This repo has no ROADMAP.md; .backlog/README.md is the single source of truth for both sequencing and scope + status.

docs.title: Migration
docs.text: At adoption time every lot (LOT-001 → LOT-011) was already shipped, so the whole monolith was migrated directly into .backlog/archive/<LOT-ID>.md compact files — no active lot directories were created. The two Typer entry-point bug fixes (previously listed "HORS LOT", named LOT-011 in the CHANGELOG) became archive/LOT-011.md. BACKLOG.md was then deleted.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• No more backlog merge conflicts; agents load only the relevant lot.
  • to-prd / to-issues work against the local backlog with no upstream fork.
  • One-time migration cost; archived shipped lots are kept compact, not split.

docs.title: Domain docs
docs.text:
Single-context repo.

  • Domain language / glossary: CONTEXT.md at the repo root.
  • Architectural decisions: docs/adr/.

Skills that read domain context (improve-codebase-architecture, diagnose, tdd) should read CONTEXT.md and consult docs/adr/ for prior decisions in the area being changed.

docs.title: Issue tracker: local .backlog/ directory
docs.text: Lots, PRDs, and tickets for this repo live as markdown under .backlog/. .backlog/ is internal working state — a dotfolder, excluded from the published MkDocs site (docs_dir is docs/).

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• One active lot per directory: .backlog/<LOT-ID>/
  • The PRD is .backlog/<LOT-ID>/PRD.md (Matt's PRD template; no separate ## Goal)
  • Tickets are .backlog/<LOT-ID>/tickets/<NN>-<slug>.md, numbered from 01 in dependency order
  • Status is a Status: line near the top of each PRD/ticket file (see triage-labels.md)
  • The lot index (Active + Archived tables of every lot + status) is .backlog/README.md, maintained by hand — there is no generator script
  • One feature branch and one PR per lot, targeting develop
  • Completed lots are moved to .backlog/archive/<LOT-ID>.md (compact, ticket table preserved, not split) once closed > 3 days

docs.title: When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"
docs.text:
• A PRD → write .backlog/<LOT-ID>/PRD.md, create the directory if needed, and add a row to the Active lots table in .backlog/README.md.
  • An issue → write .backlog/<LOT-ID>/tickets/<NN>-<slug>.md.
  • New artifacts are created at Status: ⬜ ready.

docs.title: When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"
docs.text: Read the file at the referenced path. The user normally passes the lot ID or ticket path directly.

docs.title: Archiving
docs.text: When a lot has been closed (✅ done) for more than 3 days, compact it into a single .backlog/archive/<LOT-ID>.md (a header + one ticket table), delete the .backlog/<LOT-ID>/ directory, and move its row from Active lots to Archived lots in .backlog/README.md.

docs.title: Triage labels → local Status vocabulary
docs.text:
This repo uses a single Status: line (one value at a time). Matt's five triage roles map onto it as follows:

Status Emoji Matt triage role(s) ready ⬜ ready-for-agent waiting-human 🧑 ready-for-human, needs-info wontfix 🚫 wontfix

Lifecycle-only states (no triage-role equivalent): in-progress 🔄, done ✅.

needs-triage is not used — lots are created already specified, not triaged from raw external reports. /to-prd and /to-issues create artifacts at ready ⬜.

Outils MCP exposés :

docs.title: dcs-serve.yaml
docs.text:
Ce fichier configure le serveur dcs-serve. Il est créé automatiquement au premier lancement si absent.

# Adresse et port TCP sur lesquels dcs-serve écoute les connexions depuis DCS
tcp_host: "0.0.0.0"
tcp_port: 9999

# Adresse et port HTTP/WS pour l'API REST et WebSocket
http_host: "0.0.0.0"
http_port: 8080

# Clé API (générée automatiquement au premier lancement si vide)
api_key: ""

# Timeout par défaut des commandes Lua, en secondes
default_timeout: 10.0

# Seuil de péremption du snapshot : si aucune mise à jour n'est reçue
# depuis DCS pendant ce délai, l'API renvoie 503 avec {"stale": true}
stale_threshold: 15.0

docs.title: Variables importantes
docs.text: Paramètre Défaut Description tcp_port 9999 Port TCP que le script Lua doit cibler http_port 8080 Port de l'API REST et WebSocket api_key (auto) Clé à transmettre aux clients (X-API-Key) default_timeout 10.0 Timeout des commandes exec et spawn stale_threshold 15.0 Délai avant de marquer le snapshot comme périmé

docs.title: dcs-client.yaml
docs.text:
Ce fichier configure les clients (TUI, web, MCP).

# Adresse de dcs-serve
host: "127.0.0.1"
port: 8080

# Clé API (doit correspondre à celle de dcs-serve.yaml)
api_key: "votre-cle-api"

Le fichier est recherché dans le répertoire courant ou via l'option --config.

docs.title: Script Lua
docs.text:
Le script dcs-bridge.lua se connecte à dcs-serve via TCP. Les paramètres de connexion se trouvent en tête du fichier :

local HOST = "127.0.0.1"   -- adresse de dcs-serve
local PORT = 9999           -- doit correspondre à tcp_port dans dcs-serve.yaml

Modifiez ces valeurs si DCS World et dcs-serve tournent sur des machines différentes.

docs.title: Via les binaires GitHub Releases (recommandé)
docs.text:
Téléchargez la dernière archive depuis la page GitHub Releases :

dcs-bridge-x.y.z.zip
├── dcs-serve.exe
├── dcs-client.exe
└── dcs-bridge.lua

Extrayez l'archive dans le dossier de votre choix, par exemple C:\dcs-bridge\.

docs.title: Vérification
docs.text:
.\dcs-serve.exe --help
.\dcs-client.exe --help

docs.title: Via pip
docs.text:
pip install dcs-bridge
dcs-serve --help
dcs-client --help

docs.title: Via Poetry (développement)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/VEAF/dcs-bridge.git
cd dcs-bridge
poetry install
poetry run dcs-serve --help

docs.title: Script Lua
docs.text: Copiez dcs-bridge.lua sur la machine qui héberge DCS World et injectez-le selon la méthode décrite dans les Prérequis.

docs.title: DCS World
docs.text:
dcs-bridge nécessite DCS World installé sur le serveur de mission (version Open Beta ou Stable).

Le script Lua dcs-bridge.lua doit être injecté dans chaque mission. Deux méthodes sont disponibles :

docs.title: Méthode 1 — MissionScripting.lua (persistant)
docs.text:
Ajouter la ligne suivante dans DCS World/Scripts/MissionScripting.lua :

dofile([[C:\chemin\vers\dcs-bridge.lua]])

Cette méthode charge le bridge pour toutes les missions de ce serveur.

docs.title: Méthode 2 — Trigger DO SCRIPT FILE (par mission)
docs.text:
Dans l'éditeur de mission DCS, créer un trigger :

  • Condition : Mission Start
  • Action : DO SCRIPT FILE → sélectionner dcs-bridge.lua

Cette méthode active le bridge uniquement pour la mission concernée.

docs.title: VMCT v6 (recommandé)
docs.text:
VMCT v6 est l'outil VEAF recommandé pour injecter automatiquement dcs-bridge.lua dans vos missions sans modifier MissionScripting.lua.

Consultez la documentation VEAF pour les instructions d'installation et de configuration de VMCT.

docs.title: Machine hôte de dcs-serve
docs.text:
• OS : Windows 10/11, Linux, ou macOS
  • Python : 3.11 ou supérieur (uniquement si vous installez via pip ou Poetry)
  • Réseau : le serveur DCS doit pouvoir atteindre dcs-serve sur le port TCP configuré (défaut : 9999)

docs.title: 1. Lancer dcs-serve
docs.text:
dcs-serve

Au premier lancement, dcs-serve.yaml est créé avec une clé API générée automatiquement. Notez cette clé pour la copier dans dcs-client.yaml.

INFO  TCP server listening on 0.0.0.0:9999
INFO  HTTP server listening on 0.0.0.0:8080
INFO  API key: AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUvWxYz123456

docs.title: 2. Injecter le script Lua
docs.text:
Copiez dcs-bridge.lua sur votre serveur DCS et injectez-le dans la mission (voir Prérequis).

Lancez DCS World. Dans la console de dcs-serve, vous devriez voir :

INFO  DCS connected from 127.0.0.1
INFO  Snapshot ready — 42 units

docs.title: 3. Lancer un client
docs.text:
Interface webTUI terminalServeur MCP (agents IA) 
dcs-client web

Le navigateur s'ouvre automatiquement sur http://127.0.0.1:8081 avec la carte Leaflet.

dcs-client tui

Le tableau des unités s'affiche en temps réel avec un REPL Lua intégré.

Configurez votre agent IA (Claude, etc.) pour utiliser le serveur MCP :

dcs-client mcp

Les outils disponibles : exec_lua, get_units, spawn_unit, get_mission_info.

docs.title: Configuration réseau
docs.text:
Si dcs-serve et les clients tournent sur des machines différentes, éditez dcs-client.yaml :

host: "192.168.1.100"   # adresse IP de la machine dcs-serve
port: 8080
api_key: "votre-cle-api"

docs.title: Référence API
docs.text: Toutes les routes nécessitent l'authentification via l'en-tête X-API-Key ou le paramètre de requête ?api_key=<clé>.

docs.title: Codes HTTP
docs.text: Code Signification 200 Succès (même si Lua retourne une erreur — le bridge a répondu) 503 DCS non connecté ou snapshot périmé 504 Timeout de la commande

docs.title: GET /api/units
docs.text:
Retourne la liste des unités actives depuis le snapshot.

Réponse 200

[
  {
    "name": "Enfield 1-1",
    "type": "F-16C_50",
    "coalition": 2,
    "position_dcs": {"x": 123456.0, "y": 5000.0, "z": -45678.0},
    "position_geo": {"lat": 41.123, "lon": 44.567},
    "altitude_agl": 4800.0
  }
]

Réponse 503 — DCS déconnecté ou snapshot périmé

{"detail": "DCS not connected"}

docs.title: GET /api/mission
docs.text:
Retourne les informations de la mission en cours.

Réponse 200

{"result": "Caucasus"}

docs.title: POST /api/exec
docs.text:
Exécute du code Lua arbitraire dans DCS World.

Corps de la requête

{
  "code": "return coalition.getMainTask(coalition.side.BLUE)",
  "timeout": 5.0
}

Le champ timeout est optionnel (défaut : default_timeout de dcs-serve.yaml).

Réponse 200

{"result": "42"}

ou en cas d'erreur Lua :

{"error": "attempt to index a nil value"}

Réponse 503 — DCS déconnecté

Réponse 504 — Timeout

docs.title: POST /api/spawn
docs.text:
Fait apparaître un groupe d'unités dans DCS World.

Corps de la requête

{
  "group_def": {
    "coalition": 2,
    "country": 2,
    "category": "AIRPLANE",
    "name": "Reinforcement",
    "units": [
      {
        "name": "Reinforcement-1",
        "type": "F-16C_50",
        "x": 123456.0,
        "y": -45678.0,
        "alt": 5000.0,
        "heading": 0.0
      }
    ]
  },
  "timeout": 10.0
}

Réponse 200

{"result": "42"}

Le résultat est l'identifiant du groupe spawné retourné par coalition.addGroup().

docs.title: WS /ws/stream
docs.text:
Flux d'événements en temps réel.

Authentification : paramètre de requête ?api_key=<clé>.

Connexion : à la connexion, le snapshot complet est envoyé immédiatement si le DCS est connecté.

Messages reçus

docs.title: full_refresh
docs.text:
{
  "type": "full_refresh",
  "units": [ /* tableau d'Unit */ ]
}

docs.title: unit_position
docs.text:
{
  "type": "unit_position",
  "data": { /* Unit */ }
}

docs.title: unit_spawned
docs.text:
{
  "type": "unit_spawned",
  "data": { /* Unit */ }
}

docs.title: unit_destroyed
docs.text:
{
  "type": "unit_destroyed",
  "data": {"name": "Enfield 1-1"}
}

docs.title: Modèle Unit
docs.text:
{
  "name": "string",
  "type": "string",
  "coalition": 0,
  "position_dcs": {
    "x": 0.0,
    "y": 0.0,
    "z": 0.0
  },
  "position_geo": {
    "lat": 0.0,
    "lon": 0.0
  },
  "altitude_agl": 0.0
}

coalition : 0 = Neutral, 1 = Red, 2 = Blue

docs.title: Vue d'ensemble
docs.text:
dcs-bridge est composé de trois couches indépendantes :

graph TB
    subgraph DCS["DCS World (Lua 5.1)"]
        LUA["dcs-bridge.lua\nfull_refresh toutes les 5s\névénements spontanés"]
    end

    subgraph SERVE["dcs-serve (Python asyncio)"]
        TCP["TcpHandler\nJSON newline-delimited"]
        SNAP["Snapshot\ncache en mémoire"]
        BUS["CommandBus\ncorrélation id/réponse"]
        API["FastAPI\nHTTP REST + WebSocket"]
    end

    subgraph CLIENT["dcs-client (Python)"]
        TUI["--tui\nTextual"]
        WEB["--web\nLeaflet map"]
        MCP["--mcp\nFastMCP stdio"]
    end

    LUA -->|TCP JSON \n port 9999| TCP
    TCP --> SNAP
    TCP --> BUS
    SNAP --> API
    BUS --> API
    API -->|HTTP REST| TUI
    API -->|WebSocket| TUI
    API -->|HTTP REST| WEB
    API -->|WebSocket| WEB
    API -->|HTTP REST| MCP
    MCP -->|stdio MCP| AI["Agent IA"]

docs.title: dcs-bridge.lua
docs.text:
Script Lua 5.1 exécuté dans le thread de simulation DCS. Il est appelé à chaque frame (~20 Hz) par le planificateur DCS.

  • Connexion TCP sortante vers dcs-serve (non-bloquante, settimeout(0.0001))
  • Reconnexion exponentielle (1s → 30s)
  • Envoi d'un full_refresh toutes les 5 secondes
  • Événements spontanés : unit_position, unit_spawned, unit_destroyed
  • Exécution des commandes reçues : exec (Lua arbitraire) et spawn

docs.title: dcs-serve
docs.text:
Serveur asyncio Python avec deux services co-localisés dans la même boucle d'événements :

Composant Rôle TcpHandler Accepte la connexion DCS, parse le JSON newline-delimited Snapshot Cache en mémoire des unités actives, détection de péremption CommandBus Corrélation commande/réponse par id avec timeout EventBroadcaster Fan-out thread-safe des événements vers les WebSocket clients FastAPI app Routes REST + WebSocket, middleware X-API-Key

docs.title: dcs-client
docs.text:
Trois modes indépendants partageant la même ClientConfig :

Mode Description tui Interface Textual, tableau des unités, REPL Lua web Serveur FastAPI StaticFiles + carte Leaflet JS mcp Serveur FastMCP stdio, outils pour agents IA

docs.title: Chemin montant (DCS → clients)
docs.text:
DCS World → [TCP JSON] → TcpHandler → Snapshot / EventBroadcaster
                                            ↓
                              GET /api/units  WS /ws/stream
                                            ↓
                              dcs-client tui / web / mcp

docs.title: Chemin descendant (client → DCS)
docs.text:
dcs-client mcp/tui
    ↓ POST /api/exec ou /api/spawn
FastAPI → CommandBus.register(id)
    ↓ Command JSON via TCP
dcs-bridge.lua → exécution Lua → Response JSON via TCP
    ↓
CommandBus.wait(id, timeout) → résultat au client

docs.title: Décisions d'architecture clés
docs.text:
• ADR-0001 — Conversion de coordonnées côté Lua
  • ADR-0002 — Snapshot push-based
  • ADR-0003 — Reconnexion avec backoff exponentiel

docs.title: Structure du dépôt
docs.text:
dcs-bridge/
├── src/
│   ├── dcs_bridge/
│   │   ├── common/          # Modèles Pydantic partagés, enums de protocole
│   │   ├── serve/           # dcs-serve : TCP handler, snapshot, API FastAPI
│   │   └── client/
│   │       ├── tui/         # Interface Textual
│   │       ├── web/         # Serveur HTTP + static/ (HTML/JS Leaflet)

docs.title: TDD — cycle de développement
docs.text:
dcs-bridge applique le TDD strict :

  1. Red — écrire un test qui échoue pour la fonctionnalité visée
  2. Green — implémenter le minimum de code pour faire passer le test

docs.title: Transport
docs.text:
Le protocole utilise JSON newline-delimited sur TCP. Chaque message est une ligne JSON terminée par \n.

  • Connexion : le script Lua se connecte à dcs-serve (connexion sortante depuis DCS)
  • Direction montante (DCS → serve) : full_refresh et événements spontanés
  • Direction descendante (serve → DCS) : commandes à exécuter

docs.title: full_refresh
docs.text:
Envoyé toutes les 5 secondes. Remplace atomiquement le snapshot complet.

{
  "type": "full_refresh",
  "units": [
    {
      "name": "Enfield 1-1",
      "type": "F-16C_50",
      "coalition": 2,
      "position_dcs": {"x": 123456.0, "y": 5000.0, "z": -45678.0},
      "position_geo": {"lat": 41.123, "lon": 44.567},
      "altitude_agl": 4800.0
    }
  ]
}

docs.text:
Émis à chaque changement de position significatif.

  "type": "unit_position",
  "data": {
    "name": "Enfield 1-1",
    "type": "F-16C_50",
    "coalition": 2,
    "position_dcs": {"x": 123456.0, "y": 5000.0, "z": -45678.0},
    "position_geo": {"lat": 41.123, "lon": 44.567},
    "altitude_agl": 4800.0
  }
}

docs.text:

  "type": "unit_spawned",
  "data": { /* même structure que unit_position */ }

docs.title: dcs-bridge
docs.text: dcs-bridge is a generic bridge between DCS World and external consumers (TUI, web UI, AI agents).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
graph LR
    DCS["DCS World\n(Lua bridge)"]
    SERVE["dcs-serve\n(TCP → HTTP/WS)"]
    TUI["dcs-client tui\n(Textual TUI)"]
    WEB["dcs-client web\n(Leaflet map)"]
    MCP["dcs-client mcp\n(MCP tools)"]
    AI["AI Agent\n(Claude, GPT…)"]

    DCS -->|TCP JSON| SERVE
    SERVE -->|HTTP REST| TUI
    SERVE -->|WebSocket| TUI
    SERVE -->|HTTP REST| WEB
    SERVE -->|WebSocket| WEB
    SERVE -->|HTTP REST| MCP
    MCP -->|stdio MCP| AI

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Lua bridge — injected into DCS World, streams unit positions and events in real time
  • dcs-serve — TCP/HTTP/WebSocket server, in-memory snapshot, API key authentication
  • dcs-client tui — Textual terminal UI with real-time unit table and Lua REPL
  • dcs-client web — Leaflet map with coalition-coloured markers, real-time updates
  • dcs-client mcp — MCP server exposing exec_lua, get_units, spawn_unit, get_mission_info

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# 1. Start the server
dcs-serve

# 2. Open the web UI (in another terminal)
dcs-client web

# 3. Or launch the TUI
dcs-client tui

See the Installation guide for full instructions.

docs.title: dcs-serve
docs.text:
Usage: dcs-serve [OPTIONS]

Options:
  --config PATH  Path to dcs-serve.yaml  [default: dcs-serve.yaml]
  --help         Show this message and exit

Launches the TCP server (for Lua connection) and the HTTP/WebSocket server (for clients).

docs.title: dcs-client
docs.text:
Usage: dcs-client COMMAND [OPTIONS]

Commands:
  tui   Textual terminal UI
  web   Local HTTP server with Leaflet map
  mcp   stdio MCP server for AI agents

docs.title: dcs-client tui
docs.text:
Usage: dcs-client tui [OPTIONS]

Options:
  --config PATH  Path to dcs-client.yaml  [default: dcs-client.yaml]
  --help         Show this message and exit

Launches the terminal UI with real-time unit table and Lua REPL.

TUI keyboard shortcuts:

Key Action Enter Execute Lua command Ctrl+C Quit

docs.title: dcs-client web
docs.text:
Usage: dcs-client web [OPTIONS]

Options:
  --config PATH  Path to dcs-client.yaml  [default: dcs-client.yaml]
  --port INT     Local HTTP server port    [default: 8081]
  --no-browser   Do not open the browser automatically
  --help         Show this message and exit

Launches a local HTTP server and opens the Leaflet map in the browser.

docs.title: dcs-client mcp
docs.text:
Usage: dcs-client mcp [OPTIONS]

Options:
  --config PATH  Path to dcs-client.yaml  [default: dcs-client.yaml]
  --help         Show this message and exit

Launches the MCP server on stdio. Use with an MCP-compatible AI agent.

Exposed MCP tools:

Tool Description exec_lua(code, timeout?) Execute Lua code inside DCS World get_units() Return the list of active units spawn_unit(group_def) Spawn a unit group get_mission_info() Return mission information (theatre…)

docs.title: dcs-serve.yaml
docs.text:
This file configures the dcs-serve server. It is created automatically on first launch if missing.

# TCP address and port on which dcs-serve listens for DCS connections
tcp_host: "0.0.0.0"
tcp_port: 9999

# HTTP/WS address and port for the REST API and WebSocket
http_host: "0.0.0.0"
http_port: 8080

# API key (auto-generated on first launch if empty)
api_key: ""

# Default Lua command timeout, in seconds
default_timeout: 10.0

# Snapshot staleness threshold: if no update is received from DCS
# within this delay, the API returns 503 with {"stale": true}
stale_threshold: 15.0

docs.title: Key parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description tcp_port 9999 TCP port the Lua script must target http_port 8080 REST API and WebSocket port api_key (auto) Key to pass to clients (X-API-Key) default_timeout 10.0 Timeout for exec and spawn commands stale_threshold 15.0 Delay before marking the snapshot as stale

docs.title: dcs-client.yaml
docs.text:
This file configures the clients (TUI, web, MCP).

# dcs-serve address
host: "127.0.0.1"
port: 8080

# API key (must match dcs-serve.yaml)
api_key: "your-api-key"

The file is looked up in the current directory or via the --config option.

docs.title: Lua script
docs.text:
The dcs-bridge.lua script connects to dcs-serve via TCP. Connection parameters are at the top of the file:

local HOST = "127.0.0.1"   -- dcs-serve address
local PORT = 9999           -- must match tcp_port in dcs-serve.yaml

Update these values if DCS World and dcs-serve run on different machines.

docs.title: Via GitHub Releases binaries (recommended)
docs.text:
Download the latest archive from the GitHub Releases page:

dcs-bridge-x.y.z.zip
├── dcs-serve.exe
├── dcs-client.exe
└── dcs-bridge.lua

Extract the archive to a folder of your choice, e.g. C:\dcs-bridge\.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
.\dcs-serve.exe --help
.\dcs-client.exe --help

docs.title: Via Poetry (development)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/VEAF/dcs-bridge.git
cd dcs-bridge
poetry install
poetry run dcs-serve --help

docs.title: Lua script
docs.text: Copy dcs-bridge.lua to the machine hosting DCS World and inject it using the method described in Prerequisites.

docs.title: DCS World
docs.text:
dcs-bridge requires DCS World installed on the mission server (Open Beta or Stable).

The Lua script dcs-bridge.lua must be injected into each mission. Two methods are available:

docs.title: Method 1 — MissionScripting.lua (persistent)
docs.text:
Add the following line to DCS World/Scripts/MissionScripting.lua:

dofile([[C:\path\to\dcs-bridge.lua]])

This method loads the bridge for all missions on this server.

docs.title: Method 2 — DO SCRIPT FILE trigger (per mission)
docs.text:
In the DCS mission editor, create a trigger:

  • Condition: Mission Start
  • Action: DO SCRIPT FILE → select dcs-bridge.lua

This method activates the bridge only for the specific mission.

docs.title: VMCT v6 (recommended)
docs.text:
VMCT v6 is the VEAF-recommended tool for automatically injecting dcs-bridge.lua into missions without modifying MissionScripting.lua.

See the VEAF documentation for VMCT installation and configuration instructions.

docs.title: dcs-serve host machine
docs.text:
• OS: Windows 10/11, Linux, or macOS
  • Python: 3.11 or higher (only if installing via pip or Poetry)
  • Network: the DCS server must be able to reach dcs-serve on the configured TCP port (default: 9999)

docs.title: 1. Launch dcs-serve
docs.text:
dcs-serve

On first launch, dcs-serve.yaml is created with an auto-generated API key. Copy this key into dcs-client.yaml.

INFO  TCP server listening on 0.0.0.0:9999
INFO  HTTP server listening on 0.0.0.0:8080
INFO  API key: AbCdEfGhIjKlMnOpQrStUvWxYz123456

docs.title: 2. Inject the Lua script
docs.text:
Copy dcs-bridge.lua to your DCS server and inject it into the mission (see Prerequisites).

Launch DCS World. In the dcs-serve console you should see:

INFO  DCS connected from 127.0.0.1
INFO  Snapshot ready — 42 units

docs.title: 3. Launch a client
docs.text:
Web UITerminal TUIMCP server (AI agents) 
dcs-client web

Your browser opens automatically at http://127.0.0.1:8081 with the Leaflet map.

dcs-client tui

The real-time unit table displays with an integrated Lua REPL.

Configure your AI agent (Claude, etc.) to use the MCP server:

dcs-client mcp

Available tools: exec_lua, get_units, spawn_unit, get_mission_info.

docs.title: Network configuration
docs.text:
If dcs-serve and clients run on different machines, edit dcs-client.yaml:

host: "192.168.1.100"   # IP address of the dcs-serve machine
port: 8080
api_key: "your-api-key"

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: All routes require authentication via the X-API-Key header or the ?api_key=<key> query parameter.

docs.title: HTTP codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 200 Success (even if Lua returns an error — the bridge responded) 503 DCS not connected or snapshot stale 504 Command timeout

docs.title: GET /api/units
docs.text:
Returns the list of active units from the snapshot.

Response 200

[
  {
    "name": "Enfield 1-1",
    "type": "F-16C_50",
    "coalition": 2,
    "position_dcs": {"x": 123456.0, "y": 5000.0, "z": -45678.0},
    "position_geo": {"lat": 41.123, "lon": 44.567},
    "altitude_agl": 4800.0
  }
]

Response 503 — DCS disconnected or snapshot stale

{"detail": "DCS not connected"}

docs.title: GET /api/mission
docs.text:
Returns information about the current mission.

Response 200

{"result": "Caucasus"}

docs.title: POST /api/exec
docs.text:
Executes arbitrary Lua code inside DCS World.

Request body

{
  "code": "return coalition.getMainTask(coalition.side.BLUE)",
  "timeout": 5.0
}

The timeout field is optional (default: default_timeout from dcs-serve.yaml).

Response 200

{"result": "42"}

or on Lua error:

{"error": "attempt to index a nil value"}

Response 503 — DCS disconnected

Response 504 — Timeout

docs.title: POST /api/spawn
docs.text:
Spawns a unit group in DCS World.

Request body

{
  "group_def": {
    "coalition": 2,
    "country": 2,
    "category": "AIRPLANE",
    "name": "Reinforcement",
    "units": [
      {
        "name": "Reinforcement-1",
        "type": "F-16C_50",
        "x": 123456.0,
        "y": -45678.0,
        "alt": 5000.0,
        "heading": 0.0
      }
    ]
  },
  "timeout": 10.0
}

Response 200

{"result": "42"}

The result is the spawned group identifier returned by coalition.addGroup().

docs.title: WS /ws/stream
docs.text:
Real-time event stream.

Authentication: ?api_key=<key> query parameter.

On connect: the full snapshot is sent immediately if DCS is connected.

Received messages

docs.title: full_refresh
docs.text:
{
  "type": "full_refresh",
  "units": [ /* array of Unit */ ]
}

docs.title: Unit model
docs.text:
{
  "name": "string",
  "type": "string",
  "coalition": 0,
  "position_dcs": {
    "x": 0.0,
    "y": 0.0,
    "z": 0.0
  },
  "position_geo": {
    "lat": 0.0,
    "lon": 0.0
  },
  "altitude_agl": 0.0

coalition: 0 = Neutral, 1 = Red, 2 = Blue

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
dcs-bridge is composed of three independent layers:

graph TB
    subgraph DCS["DCS World (Lua 5.1)"]
        LUA["dcs-bridge.lua\nfull_refresh every 5s\nspontaneous events"]
    end

    subgraph SERVE["dcs-serve (Python asyncio)"]
        TCP["TcpHandler\nnewline-delimited JSON"]
        SNAP["Snapshot\nin-memory cache"]
        BUS["CommandBus\nid/response correlation"]
        API["FastAPI\nHTTP REST + WebSocket"]
    end

    subgraph CLIENT["dcs-client (Python)"]
        TUI["--tui\nTextual"]
        WEB["--web\nLeaflet map"]
        MCP["--mcp\nFastMCP stdio"]
    end

    LUA -->|TCP JSON \n port 9999| TCP
    TCP --> SNAP
    TCP --> BUS
    SNAP --> API
    BUS --> API
    API -->|HTTP REST| TUI
    API -->|WebSocket| TUI
    API -->|HTTP REST| WEB
    API -->|WebSocket| WEB
    API -->|HTTP REST| MCP
    MCP -->|stdio MCP| AI["AI Agent"]

docs.title: dcs-bridge.lua
docs.text:
Lua 5.1 script running in the DCS simulation thread. It is called on every frame (~20 Hz) by the DCS scheduler.

  • Outgoing TCP connection to dcs-serve (non-blocking, settimeout(0.0001))
  • Exponential reconnect (1s → 30s)
  • Sends a full_refresh every 5 seconds
  • Spontaneous events: unit_position, unit_spawned, unit_destroyed
  • Executes received commands: exec (arbitrary Lua) and spawn

docs.title: dcs-serve
docs.text:
Python asyncio server with two services co-located in the same event loop:

Component Role TcpHandler Accepts DCS connection, parses newline-delimited JSON Snapshot In-memory cache of active units, staleness detection CommandBus Command/response correlation by id with timeout EventBroadcaster Thread-safe fan-out of events to WebSocket clients FastAPI app REST routes + WebSocket, X-API-Key middleware

docs.title: dcs-client
docs.text:
Three independent modes sharing the same ClientConfig:

Mode Description tui Textual UI, unit table, Lua REPL web FastAPI StaticFiles server + Leaflet JS map mcp FastMCP stdio server, tools for AI agents

docs.title: Upward path (DCS → clients)
docs.text:
DCS World → [TCP JSON] → TcpHandler → Snapshot / EventBroadcaster
                                            ↓
                              GET /api/units  WS /ws/stream
                                            ↓
                              dcs-client tui / web / mcp

docs.title: Downward path (client → DCS)
docs.text:
dcs-client mcp/tui
    ↓ POST /api/exec or /api/spawn
FastAPI → CommandBus.register(id)
    ↓ Command JSON via TCP
dcs-bridge.lua → Lua execution → Response JSON via TCP
    ↓
CommandBus.wait(id, timeout) → result to client

docs.title: Key architecture decisions
docs.text:
• ADR-0001 — Coordinate conversion on the Lua side
  • ADR-0002 — Push-based snapshot
  • ADR-0003 — Reconnect with exponential backoff
